s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: History of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Globe compression due to increased abscess size
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes

shortlist.label: Lacrimal sac abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies confirmed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of orbital pain, edema, and hyperemia

shortlist.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements and postseptal fat stranding

shortlist.label: Orbital apex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve and vision loss

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Potential complication of orbital infection with risk of intracranial spread

raw.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and the patient's history of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis support this diagnosis, along with the isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes, which is a common cause of abscesses.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of infection like edematous and hyperemic eyelids, the specific finding of a lacrimal sac abscess points more directly to a localized infection rather than a diffuse cellulitis.

rejected.label: Idiopathic orbital inflammatory disease
rejected.why: The presence of a specific infectious agent (Streptococcus pyogenes) and a localized abscess makes an idiopathic condition less likely.

rejected.label: Orbital apex syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves more severe symptoms including vision loss, ophthalmoplegia, and sensory deficits, which are not all present in this case.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or imaging findings typical of cavernous sinus thrombosis, such as bilateral eye involvement, cranial nerve palsies, or specific imaging evidence of thrombosis in the cavernous sinuses.

gold: Acute dacryocystitis with secondary optic nerve injury
